clickable_icon_not_iconbutton: An icon is used as a standalone interactive control through a custom clickable container or modifier instead of an appropriately accessible control such as IconButton, and equivalent button semantics, an accessible name, or a sufficient touch target are not supplied. The problem is missing accessible behavior, not the choice of IconButton itself; a custom implementation with equivalent semantics and hit area is acceptable.
color_contrast: Foreground content has insufficient luminance contrast against its actual background, making text, icons, or control boundaries difficult to perceive. Common WCAG AA thresholds are at least 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text, and 3:1 for essential non-text UI components; compliance must be evaluated against the rendered colors, including relevant themes and states.
decorative_mislabeled: An image, icon, or visual flourish that conveys no information or function is exposed to accessibility services with a content description or other announced label. This adds redundant or misleading screen-reader output; purely decorative graphics should normally use contentDescription = null or be excluded appropriately from accessibility semantics without hiding meaningful content.
error_state_no_semantics: A validation failure or other important error is communicated only visually, or its message is not accessible or associated with the affected control. Assistive-technology users may not learn what failed or how to correct it; expose understandable error text and appropriate Compose error semantics (for example, Modifier.semantics { error(...) }), with an announcement mechanism when needed.
missing_content_description: A meaningful non-text image, icon, or icon-only control lacks an accessible text alternative that communicates its purpose or content. Screen-reader users cannot reliably identify it; provide an appropriate localized contentDescription or an equivalent accessible name on its semantic parent. Decorative graphics and images already adequately described by adjacent or merged text do not need duplicate descriptions.
missing_heading_semantics: Text functions as a section or screen heading visually but is not marked programmatically as a heading in the accessibility semantics tree. This prevents assistive technologies from reliably offering heading-based navigation; mark genuine headings with Modifier.semantics { heading() }, while avoiding heading semantics on ordinary emphasized text.
missing_interaction_semantics: A UI element performs a user action but does not expose an appropriate accessibility action, enabled state, or other necessary interaction information in the Compose semantics tree. Users of TalkBack, Switch Access, or similar services may be unable to activate it or understand how it works; prefer built-in interactive components or supply clickable, toggleable, selectable, or custom accessibility actions as appropriate.
missing_merge_descendants: Multiple child composables that form one logical item are exposed as unnecessarily separate accessibility navigation targets, fragmenting a label, value, or related content and making navigation cumbersome. Where appropriate, group the information using Modifier.semantics(mergeDescendants = true) or a component with built-in merging; do not merge independently actionable children or content that must remain separately navigable.
missing_semantics_role: A custom interactive component does not communicate its control type (such as Button, Checkbox, Switch, or Tab) to accessibility services when that role cannot be inferred from built-in semantics. Without an appropriate Role, users may not know what kind of control is focused; use a suitable built-in component or assign role through Modifier.semantics or the role parameter of an interaction modifier.
missing_state_description: A stateful custom control changes between meaningful states, but its current state is not conveyed adequately through the accessibility semantics available to assistive technologies. Users may not know whether a control is selected, checked, expanded, or otherwise active; expose standard state properties such as toggleableState or selected, and provide stateDescription when a custom, understandable state label is needed. Built-in accessible state announcements are sufficient when accurate.
pointerinput_no_semantics: A custom gesture handler implemented with Modifier.pointerInput (such as tap, swipe, drag, or long press) provides functionality only through pointer gestures without an equivalent accessible action or interaction path. Assistive-technology users may be unable to discover or perform the gesture; use semantic interaction modifiers where possible or expose appropriate onClick/onLongClick or customActions alternatives.
progress_no_semantics: A progress indicator conveys a task's current progress or indeterminate activity visually but does not expose that status through accessibility semantics. Screen-reader users cannot determine progress or whether work is ongoing; use Compose progress indicators with built-in semantics or provide progressBarRangeInfo with the correct current value and range, or an indeterminate state.
text_truncation_scaling: Meaningful text is clipped, overlapped, or truncated without an accessible way to obtain the full information when the user increases system font size or display scaling. Fixed dimensions, restrictive line limits, or layouts that fail to reflow can cause this problem; allow text and containers to adapt, wrap, scroll, or otherwise provide the complete content. Intentional ellipsis is acceptable when the full information remains accessible.
textfield_no_label: A text-entry control lacks a persistent, programmatically available accessible label that identifies the expected input, leaving users dependent on visual context or placeholder text that may disappear during entry. Provide a descriptive label through TextField/OutlinedTextField label support or equivalent associated semantics; a placeholder or generic content description alone is not always a sufficient substitute.
touch_target_size: An interactive element has an effective touch target smaller than the recommended minimum of 48 dp by 48 dp, making it difficult to activate reliably for users with limited motor precision. Increase its hit area using appropriate padding, sizeIn, or accessible Material components; evaluate the interactive target rather than only the visible icon or text size.
